157|    if the length of *iterable* is not divisible by *n*:

165|    ``True``, then ``ValueError`` will be raised before the last
166|    list is yielded.

258|class peekable:
259|    """Wrap an iterator to allow lookahead and prepending elements.

261|    Call :meth:`peek` on the result to get the value that will be returned
262|    by :func:`next`. This won't advance the iterator:
263|
264|        >>> p = peekable(['a', 'b'])
265|        >>> p.peek()
266|        'a'
267|        >>> next(p)
268|        'a'
269|
270|    Pass :meth:`peek` a default value to return that instead of raising
271|    ``StopIteration`` when the iterator is exhausted.
272|
273|        >>> p = peekable([])
274|        >>> p.peek('hi')
275|        'hi'
276|
277|    peekables also offer a :meth:`prepend` method, which "inserts" items
278|    at the head of the iterable:
279|
280|        >>> p = peekable([1, 2, 3])
281|        >>> p.prepend(10, 11, 12)
282|        >>> next(p)
283|        10
284|        >>> p.peek()
285|        11
286|        >>> list(p)
287|        [11, 12, 1, 2, 3]
288|
289|    peekables can be indexed. Index 0 is the item that will be returned by
290|    :func:`next`, index 1 is the item after that, and so on:
291|    The values up to the given index will be cached.
292|
293|        >>> p = peekable(['a', 'b', 'c', 'd'])
294|        >>> p[0]
295|        'a'
296|        >>> p[1]
297|        'b'
298|        >>> next(p)
299|        'a'
300|
301|    Negative indexes are supported, but be aware that they will cache the
302|    remaining items in the source iterator, which may require significant
303|    storage.
304|
305|    To check whether a peekable is exhausted, check its truth value:
306|
307|        >>> p = peekable(['a', 'b'])
308|        >>> if p:  # peekable has items
309|        ...     list(p)
310|        ['a', 'b']
311|        >>> if not p:  # peekable is exhausted
312|        ...     list(p)
313|        []
314|
315|    """

317|    def __init__(self, iterable):
318|        self._it = iter(iterable)
319|        self._cache = deque()
320|
321|    def __iter__(self):
322|        return self
323|
324|    def __bool__(self):
325|        try:
326|            self.peek()
327|        except StopIteration:
328|            return False
329|        return True

331|    def peek(self, default=_marker):
332|        """Return the item that will be next returned from ``next()``.
333|
334|        Return ``default`` if there are no items left. If ``default`` is not
335|        provided, raise ``StopIteration``.
336|
337|        """
338|        if not self._cache:
339|            try:
340|                self._cache.append(next(self._it))
341|            except StopIteration:
342|                if default is _marker:
343|                    raise
344|                return default
345|        return self._cache[0]

347|    def prepend(self, *items):
348|        """Stack up items to be the next ones returned from ``next()`` or
349|        ``self.peek()``. The items will be returned in
350|        first in, first out order::
351|
352|            >>> p = peekable([1, 2, 3])
353|            >>> p.prepend(10, 11, 12)
354|            >>> next(p)
355|            10
356|            >>> list(p)
357|            [11, 12, 1, 2, 3]
358|
359|        It is possible, by prepending items, to "resurrect" a peekable that
360|        previously raised ``StopIteration``.
361|
362|            >>> p = peekable([])
363|            >>> next(p)
364|            Traceback (most recent call last):
365|              ...
366|            StopIteration
367|            >>> p.prepend(1)
368|            >>> next(p)
369|            1
370|            >>> next(p)
371|            Traceback (most recent call last):
372|              ...
373|            StopIteration
374|
375|        """
376|        self._cache.extendleft(reversed(items))
377|
378|    def __next__(self):
379|        if self._cache:
380|            return self._cache.popleft()
381|
382|        return next(self._it)

384|    def _get_slice(self, index):
385|        # Normalize the slice's arguments
386|        step = 1 if (index.step is None) else index.step
387|        if step > 0:
388|            start = 0 if (index.start is None) else index.start
389|            stop = maxsize if (index.stop is None) else index.stop
390|        elif step < 0:
391|            start = -1 if (index.start is None) else index.start

397|        # the rest of the iterable in order to slice from the right side.

429|        ... def tally():

433|        ...         i += 1

436|        >>> t.send('red')
